name: MediaIntelligence
summary: Analyze video content and group faces in images using on-device machine learning.

declarations.name: FaceGroupAnalyzer
declarations.comment:
An object that detects faces in images and groups them by person.

``FaceGroupAnalyzer`` is the central object in the face analysis
pipeline. It detects faces in images, stores their data
persistently in a working directory you choose, and clusters the faces
into groups called *entities*, where each entity represents a
distinct person.

The analyzer stores all face data and cluster assignments in the
directory you pass to ``FaceGroupAnalyzer/init(workingDirectory:)``.
This directory persists between app launches, so subsequent runs resume
from where the previous session ended. Call
``FaceGroupAnalyzer/purge(workingDirectory:)`` to remove all data from
the directory.

Use ``FaceGroupAnalyzer/identifyFaces(in:)`` to detect and match faces
in images without storing anything. This is useful for recognizing
people in new images against an existing gallery without modifying the
analyzer's data.

members.signature: final nonisolated(nonsending) func identifyFaces(in assets: [MediaIntelligenceImageAsset]) async throws -> some AsyncSequence<(assetID: MediaIntelligenceImageAsset.ID, faces: Array<FaceGroupAnalyzer.Face>), any Error>
members.comment:
Detects and identifies faces without modifying the analyzer's data.

Use this method to recognize people in new images against the
existing gallery without storing any face data. Each returned face
has an ``FaceGroupAnalyzer/Face/entityID`` if the framework matched
it to a known entity, or `nil` if no match was found.

- Parameter assets: The image assets to analyze.
- Returns: An async sequence of `(assetID, faces)` pairs.

members.signature: final var allFacesByEntityID: some AsyncSequence<(entityID: FaceGroupAnalyzer.Entity.ID, faces: Array<FaceGroupAnalyzer.Face>), any Error> { get }

members.name: insertOrUpdateAssets
members.signature: final nonisolated(nonsending) func insertOrUpdateAssets(_ assets: [MediaIntelligenceImageAsset]) async throws -> some AsyncSequence<(assetID: MediaIntelligenceImageAsset.ID, faces: Array<FaceGroupAnalyzer.Face>), any Error>
members.comment:
Adds or replaces image assets in the analyzer.

For each asset, the method detects faces and extracts facial data,
then persists the results to the working directory. If an asset
with the same identifier already exists, the method replaces its
face data.

After this call, ``FaceGroupAnalyzer/state`` becomes
``FaceGroupAnalyzer/State/stale`` until you call
``FaceGroupAnalyzer/update(subprogress:)``. Faces detected in this
call have a `nil` ``FaceGroupAnalyzer/Face/entityID`` until
clustering runs.

- Parameter assets: The image assets to ingest.
- Returns: An async sequence of `(assetID, faces)` pairs — one per
  asset — reporting the faces detected in each image.

declarations.name: FaceGroupAnalyzer.Entity
declarations.comment:
A cluster of faces that belong to the same person.

This type represents a distinct person as
identified by the framework's clustering algorithm. After you call
``FaceGroupAnalyzer/update(subprogress:)``, each detected face
receives a ``FaceGroupAnalyzer/Face/entityID`` that associates it
with an entity.

Use ``FaceGroupAnalyzer/fetchFaces(for:)`` to retrieve all faces
that belong to a particular entity, or
``FaceGroupAnalyzer/fetchAssetIDs(for:)`` to find the images in
which a person appears.

declarations.name: FaceGroupAnalyzer.Face
declarations.comment:
A face detected in an image asset.

This type represents a single face that ``FaceGroupAnalyzer``
detects in an image. It records the face's
location within the image, the identifier of the image it came
from, and after ``FaceGroupAnalyzer/update(subprogress:)`` runs,
the entity the face belongs to.

The ``FaceGroupAnalyzer/Face/bounds`` rectangle uses normalized
coordinates in the range `0.0` to `1.0` along both axes, with the
origin at the top-left corner of the image.

members.name: id
members.comment: A unique identifier for the face.

members.name: bounds
members.comment:
A normalized rectangle describing the location of the face within its source image.

The rectangle uses normalized coordinates, where `0.0` is the
top-left corner and `1.0` is the bottom-right corner along each
axis.
members.typescript: get bounds(): { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }

members.name: assetID
members.comment: An identifier for the image asset that contains this face.

members.name: entityID
members.comment:
An identifier for the entity this face belongs to.

This value is `nil` until you call
``FaceGroupAnalyzer/update(subprogress:)``. After clustering
runs, every face receives an entity identifier that groups it
with other faces of the same person.

declarations.name: HighlightAnalysisRequest
declarations.comment:
A request that identifies the most engaging segments of a video.

``HighlightAnalysisRequest`` asks ``VideoAnalyzer`` to find the highlight
segments of a video and score every segment for engagement. Pass it to
``VideoAnalyzer/analyze(_:for:)`` to receive a
``HighlightAnalysisRequest/Result`` value.

members.name: init
members.comment: Creates a highlight analysis request.

declarations.name: HighlightAnalysisRequest.Result
declarations.comment:
The output of a highlight analysis.

This type describes the highlights and
engagement levels the framework finds in a video.

``HighlightAnalysisRequest/Result/highlights`` lists the time ranges
the framework identifies as highlights. Use these ranges to build a
highlight reel or to seek directly to the most interesting moments.

``HighlightAnalysisRequest/Result/levels`` provides a finer-grained
view where every segment in the video gets a floating-point engagement
level from `0` (least engaging) to `9` (most engaging). Use these
values to visualize a video's pacing or to let people scrub through
segments by interest level.

members.name: highlights
members.comment: The time ranges the framework identifies as highlights.

members.name: levels
members.comment:
The engagement level of each segment in the video.

Each element pairs a <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/coremedia/cmtimerange>
with a floating-point level value from `0` (least engaging) to
`9` (most engaging). The array covers every segment in the video,
not just the highlights.

declarations.name: KeyFrameAnalysisRequest
declarations.comment:
A request that identifies the best representative frame of a video.

Use this type to find the single frame that best represents the
overall content of the video. Pass it to
``VideoAnalyzer/analyze(_:for:)`` to receive a
``KeyFrameAnalysisRequest/Result`` value containing the frame's
timestamp.

Use the timestamp to seek a player to that position or to
extract a thumbnail image.

members.name: init
members.comment: Creates a key frame analysis request.

declarations.name: KeyFrameAnalysisRequest.Result
declarations.comment:
The output of a key frame analysis.

``KeyFrameAnalysisRequest/Result`` contains the timestamp of the
frame the framework selects as the best representative of the video.
Use this <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/coremedia/cmtime>
value to seek a player to that position or to extract a thumbnail.

members.name: timestamp
members.comment: The timestamp of the key frame.

declarations.name: MediaIntelligenceImageAsset
declarations.comment:
An image asset to analyze.

Create a ``MediaIntelligenceImageAsset`` to identify an image you want
``FaceGroupAnalyzer`` to process. Each asset has a unique identifier
you assign, and a ``MediaIntelligenceImageAsset/Kind`` value that
describes how the framework accesses the image data.

Use the same ``MediaIntelligenceImageAsset/ID`` value consistently for
a specified image. The framework uses this identifier to match new
submissions against existing data, so changing the identifier causes
the framework to treat the image as a new asset.

members.name: init
members.comment:
Creates an image asset with the specified identifier and kind.

- Parameters:
  - id: A unique identifier for the asset.
  - kind: A value that describes how the framework accesses the
    image data.
members.typescript: static init(id: MediaIntelligenceImageAsset_ID, kind: MediaIntelligenceImageAsset_Kind): MediaIntelligenceImageAsset

members.name: id
members.comment: A unique identifier for the asset.

members.name: kind
members.comment: A value that describes how the framework accesses the image data.

declarations.name: MediaIntelligenceImageAsset.ID
declarations.comment:
A unique identifier for an image asset.

``MediaIntelligenceImageAsset/ID`` is a string-backed identifier
you assign to each image asset. The framework uses this value to
track assets across calls to
``FaceGroupAnalyzer/insertOrUpdateAssets(_:)`` and
``FaceGroupAnalyzer/deleteAssets(_:)``.

Choose identifiers that remain constant for a specified image. For
example, a photo library asset identifier or a file path that
doesn't change.

declarations.name: VideoAnalyzer
declarations.comment:
An object that analyzes video assets for highlights and key frames.

A video analyzer is the central object in the video analysis pipeline.
Access it through the static ``VideoAnalyzer/shared`` property and pass it a
``MediaIntelligenceVideoAsset`` along with one or more request objects.
The analyzer processes the video and returns a tuple containing one
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/swift/result> per request, in the same order you provide them.

members.name: shared
members.comment: The shared video analyzer.

declarations.name: VideoAnalyzer.Request
declarations.comment:
A type that describes a video analysis operation.

The framework provides two built-in request types:
``HighlightAnalysisRequest`` and ``KeyFrameAnalysisRequest``.

declarations.name: VideoAnalyzer.Result
declarations.comment:
A type that represents the output of a video analysis operation.

This type is the base protocol for analysis result types. You
receive a typed value conforming to this protocol when
``VideoAnalyzer/analyze(_:for:)`` succeeds for a particular
request. The framework uses the request's associated
``VideoAnalyzer/Request/Result`` type to determine the concrete
type returned for each element in the tuple.
